cells.tense: You are here, and what you recognize in people is being spent with the people sitting across from you.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Before you decide how a conversation with someone close will go, sit with the pull you feel toward them and give it one beat more than you usually allow before you speak.
cells.core:
You can recognize what's happening between people before anyone says it, and then stay beside them while they arrive at it themselves. That's the thing working well: you catch the pattern, and you don't paste it on the person. You let them reach it. The connection holds because you aren't ahead of them, you're with them.

This week, give the pull its moment before you act on it. When you're sitting with someone who matters, notice what draws you toward them and don't name the pattern or correct the course yet. Wait one beat more than usual. The recognition will still be there when you come back to it, and the other person gets to be part of how it's understood. That's the whole practice.
cells.sheetLine: You see the pattern and still stand beside someone.
cells.verb: SEEING THE PATTERN AND SPENDING IT WHERE IT CAN CONNECT
cells.place: WHERE YOU STAND WITH THE PEOPLE CLOSE TO YOU

cells.tense: You are bracing for a room you can't write in advance, and the pattern-recognition is hot in your hands.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Pick the conversation with someone close that you've been rehearsing in your head, and have it this week — say what you want, no refinements, no pre-checking their face.
cells.core:
Your eye for a relationship is quick, and when it's working you can say 'this is what's happening between us' and it frees people. But the sharpness has no floor under it at this pass. You're reading people down to the shape of them, and the reading runs faster than the conversation, sorting before anyone has arrived. Connection comes after your analysis, so you're already with them once you've decided who they are.

What's needed isn't more insight. It's a clear structure to carry what you already see. Decide which relationship you've been turning over and make the call about what to do with it. Carry it through the same day. The structure will hold what your eye catches, instead of your eye holding both of you.
cells.sheetLine: You read through people and call it being with them.

cells.tense: They are still standing at a door that's already behind them, and the quick analysis is loud in a quiet room.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: Think of one interaction you keep up out of habit that no longer connects you, and skip it this week — or replace it with a call that asks something real of both of you.
cells.core:
You can spot the pattern in what someone's saying, and that part is still sharp. But your link to the person actually across the table is running low — analysis is cheaper and easier, so you answer with what you know about them instead of with the connection itself. You notice the shape of the conversation and not the person in it. They feel it. You tell yourself you're tired, or busy, and both are true, but neither is the whole of it.

There's a way through people, not through the puzzle. Find a routine connection that's gone hollow and put it down — or turn it into a real exchange that asks something of both of you. Not more effort in your head. A walk toward the living thing. The link starts there, where someone can meet you.

cells.tense: You're doing the work of connection and filing it under a name that isn't yours to keep.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: The next time someone close stirs something in you, follow that feeling a little way — stay with it for a moment before you turn it into a verdict or set it down.
cells.core:
You hold more possible feeling about the people in your life than you let yourself notice. There's a pull toward certain people, and you act on it — the message sent, the invitation made, the room you walk into — and then you set it down as nothing, or circumstance, or just being polite. What you did was real. You just haven't put your name on it.

Let that pull be felt before it gets turned into analysis. Next time someone close stirs something in you, follow it a little way and look at it up close — no verdict, no sorting, no essay afterward. Let the connection be what it is before you name it. Your name belongs on it. It has been there the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: The pull toward people is yours, and you've been filing it under nothing.
cells.verb: SEEING THE PATTERN AND SPENDING IT WHERE IT CAN CONNECT
cells.place: WHERE YOU STAND WITH THE PEOPLE CLOSE TO YOU

attempts.check: I claim this person's fast pattern-sight is costing their steady link to others, that they see through people now instead of beside them. The record does not cover history and may be wrong about the cause — the reader could rightly say the reading is of someone burned by people, not of a mind in excess. The ask still works if the read is wrong: it makes the person spend time on connection that they perceive as living and un-forced. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'you look through people and call it looking at them' — it is sharp, it sounds insightful, and I will keep it out of the core because it explains their life rather than offers them something they can refuse.
